title: JSON Schema for NeoLoad as-code files

$schema.description: Optional URL of the JSON Schema used by editors to validate the file. It is ignored when the project is loaded.

schemaVersion.description: Schema contract version this file is written for. Must be 3.1 as a string or number for this schema.

name.description: The root key defining the name of the project.

includes.title: Includes
includes.description: Other as-code files loaded before this one. Each entry is a path relative to the project folder and must be inside the project folder. It declares the same top-level elements as a project file.

variables.title: Variables

sql.description: A list or table of values loaded from the result of a SQL query executed on a database.

shared_queue.description: A queue shared between virtual users, usable as a producer/consumer channel, with optional persistence to a file.

secret_vault.description: A reference to a secret stored in an external vault provider configured in NeoLoad Web (HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager). The provider type is resolved server-side from provider_id; it is not stored in the as-code file.

variables.description: Variables add dynamic content to a scenario. They can be combined with other variables or with static content, for example `${product_${productID}}`, and used in places such as form parameter values.

servers.title: Servers
servers.description: Target servers for the test, defined once so the host can be changed without editing each request.

sla_profiles.title: SLA Profiles
sla_profiles.description: Service level agreement profiles. Each profile is a set of KPI thresholds used to check quality of service, for example a maximum average response time.

populations.title: Populations
populations.description: Groups of Virtual Users. Each population lists the User Paths that compose it and the share of each one.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.description: Test configurations. A scenario selects the populations to run and the load policy of each one.

shared_elements.title: Shared_elements
shared_elements.description: Named, reusable steps declared once for the project. A shared_element step runs one of them by name.

user_paths.title: User_paths
user_paths.description: Virtual user behavior. A User Path is the sequence of requests and logical actions that simulates one visitor.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.description: Threshold list. Each KPI+scope combination must appear at most once.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description:
Format: [kpi] (warn|fail) >=|==|<= [value][unit] ... per test|interval

Multiple conditions (warn and/or fail) can be combined on the same line. Units: s, ms, /s, Mbps, MB, %.

KPIs per test:
  avg-request-resp-time    — average request response time (s, ms)
  avg-page-resp-time       — average page response time (s, ms)
  avg-transaction-resp-time — average transaction response time (s, ms)
  perc-transaction-resp-time (p{N}) — Nth-percentile transaction response time, default p90 (s, ms)
  avg-request-per-sec      — average requests per second (/s)
  avg-throughput-per-sec   — average throughput per second (Mbps)
  errors-count             — total number of errors
  count                    — total element count
  throughput               — total throughput (MB)
  error-rate               — error rate (%)

KPIs per interval:
  avg-resp-time            — average response time (s, ms)
  avg-elt-per-sec          — average elements per second (/s)
  avg-throughput-per-sec   — average throughput per second (Mbps)
  errors-per-sec           — errors per second (/s)
  error-rate               — error rate (%)

if.description: A conditional structure "If - Then - Else". If the conditions are true, the Then container is executed, otherwise, the Else container is executed.

while.description: A repetition structure "While - do". The steps contained in the structure are executed in sequence until the condition is not verified any more.

It allows the Switch value to change the control flow of the User Path execution via a multiway branch, named Case statements. The Switch action is fall-through, which means that if a Break flag is disabled on a Case, then the next Case statement is executed.

browser_open.description: Real Browser action BrowserOpen. Open a new browser.

browser_close.description: Real Browser action BrowserClose. Close the browser. This action is useful for avoiding stacking browser instances on a single VU. The recommended configurations is : If the OpenBrowser action is at the beginning of the ACTIONS container, put the CloseBrowser action at end of the ACTIONS container.

browser_navigate.description: Real Browser action BrowserNavigate. Navigate to an url.

browser_click.description: Real Browser action BrowserClick. Click a selector.

browser_type.description: Real Browser action BrowserType. Type some text inside an element.

browser_press.description: Real Browser action BrowserPress. Press a key on a selector.

browser_select_option.description: Real Browser action BrowserSelectOption. Select one or several options of a select element.

browser_mouse_over.description: Real Browser action BrowserMouseOver. Positions the mouse over the specified coordinates or element location. Scrolls the window when that position is out of the current viewport. Both parameters can be set at the same time, in that case the mouse will be positioned at the specified coordinates relative to the located element instead of the page origin.

browser_drag_and_drop.description: Real Browser action BrowserDragAndDrop. Drag and drop an element onto another element.

browser_scroll.description: Real Browser action BrowserScroll. Scrolls the window to a particular place in the document.

browser_read.description: Real Browser action BrowserRead. Read the text content of an Element.

browser_wait_selector.description: Real Browser action BrowserWaitSelector. Wait for a selector.

browser_evaluate_javascript.description: Real Browser action BrowserEvaluateJavascript. Executes some arbitrary Javascript code in the current page context.

browser_upload_file.description: Real Browser action BrowserUploadFile. Upload files to an input element.

browser_handle_dialog.description: Real Browser action BrowserHandleDialog. Set dialog behavior.

browser_open_tab.description: Real Browser action BrowserOpenTab. Open a new tab at the rightmost position.

browser_switch_tab.description: Real Browser action BrowserSwitchTab. Switch tab to the given index.

browser_close_tab.description: Real Browser action BrowserCloseTab. Close tab at the given index.

browser_capture_requests.description: Real Browser action BrowserCaptureRequests. Configure the capture of HTTP requests metrics for analysis purpose. It allows to capture the metrics (duration, TTFB, success...) of the requests sent and responses received between the browser and the server. By default when no regexp/url/resourceType parameter is specified, then all the HTTP request metrics are aggregated in a single group. When a matching criteria is defined (regexp/url/resourceType), the metrics of all HTTP requests matching it are aggregated in a group, and the non-matching one in a different group (for example with regexp (.*)\.html then requests will be split in two different groups: one for all HTML pages and another one for all other resources). When multiple matching criteria are defined (regexp/url/resourceType), they are applied in order they are defined.

browser_capture_web_vitals.description: Real Browser action BrowserCaptureWebVitals. Captures Core Web Vitals metrics during Virtual User navigation. This helps detect performance issues that affect the user experience. NeoLoad collects the following metrics for each defined URL: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). If you don't define a URL, NeoLoad aggregates metrics across all visited pages. To collect all metrics, place this action before the first Navigate action. The Virtual User needs to stay a minimum amount of time and perform at least one interaction to ensure Web Vitals were collected for a given page.

try_catch.description: A logical action that executes a Try container and, if one of the caught exception types occurs while running it, executes the Catch container.

fork.description: The Fork action is used to play actions in a different execution thread to the current one. This execution thread is parallel to the main chain used by the Virtual User. When the current iteration of the Virtual User stops, all the threads created using Fork actions in the Actions Container are immediately halted.

wait_until.description: The Wait Until action pauses the current execution thread until certain conditions have been verified. You may also set a maximum timeout delay: once this delay is timed out, the thread is restarted and the following action is executed, even if the conditions have not been verified.

variable_modifier.description: A Variable Modifier action makes it possible to change the value of a variable separately from its value changing policy. For example, the value of a variable may be modified in a loop for a User Path.

debug_logger.description: The Debug Logger Action writes a text entry to a log file, for debugging purposes.

rendezvous.description: A Rendezvous point synchronizes Virtual Users at a common meeting point so they carry out tasks simultaneously, creating an intense load on the server at a specific point in the application.

stop_vu.description: The Stop Virtual User action stops the current virtual user. By default, a new virtual user is started to replace the one that has been stopped, so that the number of running virtual users remains stable. Set `start_new_vu` to `false` to stop the current virtual user without starting a replacement.

web_page.description: The Web Page Action is used to group together the requests and resources that make up a single page load, along with options controlling how its resources are played back.

shared_element.description: The name of the shared_elements entry to run here.

websocket_channel.description: The WebSocket Channel action opens a WebSocket connection (HTTP upgrade) and keeps it open for the rest of the iteration. It is defined like a request (`url`, `server`, `headers`, `extractors`) plus `messages_mapping`, `timestamp_extractor` and `push_messages`. A channel is designated by its complete path, written in the `channel` property of a websocket_request.

websocket_request.description: The WebSocket Request action sends a frame (text, binary or close) on a channel opened earlier by a websocket_channel of the same user path. It is asynchronous unless `synchronous` is true, in which case it waits for the response frame whose correlation id equals `mapping_id`.

web_page.title: Action: Web Page

name.description: The Web Page name. Defaults to `web_page`

sla_profile.description: The name of the SLA profile to apply to the Web Page (will not be applied to children)

think_time.description: The think time to apply before playing the Web Page. Same syntax as the pacing.

playback.description: How the Web Page's steps are played. The default is `parallel`.

execute_resources.description: How the Web Page's resources are executed. The default is `static`.

steps.description: Steps of the Web Page. Only request and nested `web_page` steps are supported

web_page.description: The Web Page Action is used to group together the requests and resources that make up a single page load, along with options controlling how its resources are played back.

websocket_channel.title: Action: WebSocket Channel
websocket_channel.description: The WebSocket Channel action opens a WebSocket connection (HTTP upgrade) and keeps it open for the rest of the iteration. It is defined like a request (`url`, `server`, `headers`, `extractors`) plus `messages_mapping`, `timestamp_extractor` and `push_messages`. A channel is designated by its complete path, written in the `channel` property of a websocket_request.

url.description: The channel URL, with the `http` or `https` scheme (`ws` and `wss` are not accepted), or a path relative to `server`. Variables are accepted.

server.description: The name of a server defined in `servers`, used when `url` is a relative path.

headers.description: Headers of the upgrade request, as a list of single-entry maps (`Header-Name: value`). `Upgrade: websocket` is implied and does not need to be written.

extractors.description: Variable extractors applied to the response of the upgrade request.

content_assertions.description: The list of assertions to validate the response of the upgrade request

duration_assertion.description: Checks that the upgrade request completed within a given duration

size_assertion.description: Checks the length of the response content, in bytes.

messages_mapping.description: How to extract the correlation id from each inbound frame. It is compared with the `mapping_id` of a synchronous websocket_request. Mandatory as soon as a synchronous websocket_request uses this channel.

timestamp_extractor.description: Where the time the server sent a frame is found in the frame, as a number of milliseconds since the epoch. It is the start time of the push message that handles the frame; without it the push message is measured from the reception of the frame, which gives a time of zero.

push_messages.description: The handlers of the frames the channel receives. A frame that answers a waiting synchronous websocket_request goes to that request and no push message runs. Otherwise every push message whose `conditions` are true runs, in order; only if none matched, every push message without `conditions` (the fallbacks) runs.

websocket_request.title: Action: WebSocket Request
websocket_request.description: The WebSocket Request action sends a frame (text, binary or close) on a channel opened earlier by a websocket_channel of the same user path. It is asynchronous unless `synchronous` is true, in which case it waits for the response frame whose correlation id equals `mapping_id`.

message_type.description: The kind of frame: `text` (default), `binary` or `close`. A `close` ends the connection: it cannot be synchronous, and may carry a `status_code` and a reason in `body`.

synchronous.description: When true, the request waits for the inbound frame whose correlation id equals `mapping_id`; the channel must then declare `messages_mapping`. Defaults to false. WARNING: inside a push message, a synchronous request must be inside a `fork`, otherwise it blocks the thread that receives the frames and fails after `runtime.so.timeout`.

mapping_id.description: The correlation id of the awaited response. Required when `synchronous` is true, and only allowed then. Variables are accepted.

status_code.description: The close status code, only for a `close`. Defaults to 1000 (normal closure).

body.description: The frame content as text, or the reason of a `close`. Mutually exclusive with `bodybinary`.

bodybinary.description: The frame content as Base64, for a binary frame. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

extractors.description: Variable extractors applied to the response, only for a synchronous request.

content_assertions.description: Content assertions applied to the response, only for a synchronous request.

duration_assertion.description: Checks that the response was received within a given duration, only for a synchronous request.

size_assertion.description: Checks the length of the response content, in bytes, only for a synchronous request.

allOf.$comment: Only a synchronous request has a response: it needs mapping_id, and only it may carry mapping_id, extractors and content_assertions
A close cannot be synchronous, and only a close may set a status_code other than the default

websocket_channel_reference.title: WebSocket Channel Reference
websocket_channel_reference.description: The complete path of the channel to use: segments joined with '>', with no space around it. It starts with where the channel is declared: init, actions or end for a channel declared in a user path, or shared_elements>SharedElementName for one declared inside a shared element. Then comes the name of each step on the way down to the channel (for instance a transaction, a loop, a while or a fork), and last the name of the channel itself. Fixed segments: the branches of an if are then and else; the branches of a try_catch are try and catch; the default branch of a switch is default, while a switch case is designated by its name. A channel declared inside a push message is designated by the name of the outer channel, then the name of the push message (push_messages and steps are keys, not segments). A shared_element step is not part of a path. Two sibling steps on the path must not share a name. A request can only use a channel of its own user path.

websocket_push_message.title: WebSocket Push Message
websocket_push_message.description: A handler of the frames received by its channel. With conditions it runs when they are true; without conditions it is a fallback, which runs only when no push message with conditions matched

conditions.description: The conditions on the frame, written like those of an `if`; at least one when present. The variable `${NL-MessageContent}` holds the content of the frame. Without `conditions` the push message is a fallback.

match.description: How the `conditions` are combined: `any` (default) or `all`. Only allowed with `conditions`.

extractors.description: Variable extractors applied to the frame, before `steps` run.

content_assertions.description: Content assertions applied to the frame.

duration_assertion.description: Checks the duration of the push message.

size_assertion.description: Checks the length of the frame content, in bytes.

steps.description: The steps to run for a matching frame; may be empty. These steps run on the thread that receives the frames of the channel, so a long action should be inside a `fork`. A synchronous websocket_request must always be inside a `fork`: otherwise it waits for a frame that this thread cannot deliver, and fails after `runtime.so.timeout`.

websocket_messages_mapping.title: WebSocket Messages Mapping
websocket_messages_mapping.description: Tells a channel how to extract the correlation id from an inbound frame. The extracted value is compared with the `mapping_id` of a synchronous websocket_request to pair a response with the request waiting for it. `xpath` and `jsonpath` are mutually exclusive.

xpath.description: XPath expression applied to the frame. Mutually exclusive with `jsonpath`.

jsonpath.description: JSONPath expression applied to the frame. Mutually exclusive with `xpath`.

regexp.description: Regular expression applied to the frame, or to the `xpath` / `jsonpath` result. Defaults to `(.*)`.

template.description: Template applied to the result of `regexp`: `$1$` is the first captured group, `$2$` the second. Defaults to `$1$`.

websocket_timestamp_extractor.title: WebSocket Timestamp Extractor
websocket_timestamp_extractor.description: Finds, in each inbound frame, the time the server sent it, as a number of milliseconds since the epoch. It is the start time of the push message that handles the frame. The clocks of the server and of the load generator must be synchronized: a value that is not a number, or that is in the future, gives a time of zero.

regexp.description: Regular expression applied to the content of the frame.

template.description: Builds the value from the groups `regexp` captured: `$1$` is the first group, `$2$` the second, any other text is kept as it is. Defaults to `$1$`.

value.description: The text content of the part

filename.description: The file name sent to the server

source_filename.description: The path of the file used as part content, relative to the project folder. The file must be inside the project folder.

from.description: The part of the response the value is extracted from.

xpath.description: The XPath expression where to extract value. Only available when "from" value is "body".

jsonpath.description: The JSONPath expression where to extract value. Only available when "from" value is "body".

regexp.description: The regular expression applies on "from" value. If "Body" and "xpath" or "jsonpath" is specified, then the extraction is done on the result of the xpath or jsonpath. The default value is "(.*)".

match_number.description: If multiple values have matched "regexp", the match number defines which match to use. Value "-1" is to extract all occurrences, "0" to randomly extract one occurence and "N" to extract the Nth occurrence. The default value is "1".

template.description: The template used to construct the value. This is an arbitrary string containing special elements that refer to groups within the regular expression (a group is a dynamic portion of the regular expression set within brackets): $0$ refers to the entire text matching the expression, $1$ refers to group 1, $2$ refers to group 2, and so on. The default value is $1$.

decode.description: Decoder applied to the extracted value.

extract_once.description: When true, only the first extracted value is kept.

default.description: The value to return when not extracted. The default value is "<NOT FOUND>".

throw_assertion_error.description: Raises an assertion error when no match found. The default value is "true".

extractor.description: Extractors allow chaining several API calls where the argument of a call can be extracted from a previous call.

xpath.description: The validation check will be carried out on one of the nodes in the response body. This node is defined using XPath expression.

jsonpath.description: The validation check will be carried out on one of the nodes in the response body. This node is defined using JSONPath expression.

not.description: Checks whether or not the server response contains a certain content. The default value is "false".

contains.description: The validation check will be carried out on the response headers and body. If "xpath" or "jsonpath" is specified, then the validation is done on the result of the XPath or JSONPath expression.

regexp.description: This option allows considering that the "contains" value is a regular expression. The default value is "false".

equals.description: The response size must be exactly this number of bytes

greater_than.description: The response size must be strictly greater than this size, in bytes

less_than.description: The response size must be strictly lower than this size, in bytes

duration_assertion.title: Duration Assertion

less_than.description: The maximum allowed duration, in milliseconds.

duration_assertion.description: A duration assertion checks that a request or custom_action completed within a given duration. The step is considered failed if its execution time is greater than or equal to `less_than`.

pacing.description: The minimum duration enforced for the case. A random pacing `max` must be greater than or equal to `min`.

sla_profile.description: The name of the SLA profile to apply to the Case (will not be applied to children)

assertions.description: The list of assertions to validate the response content of all requests matching criteria within the Container. By default, the validation is applied only on response with content-type text/html or text/xhtml. List of content-types used for response matching can be customized in the Project Settings / Runtime Parameters from the GUI project (cannot be customized with As-code only project).

name.description: The name of the parameter, as expected by the action

type.description: A `PASSWORD` value is stored encrypted in the NeoLoad project.

name.description: The name of the action. Defaults to the action type, for example `BrowserClick`.

asRequest.description: Consider the executions as requests in the calculation of the statistics and graphs

duration_assertion.description: Checks that the action completed within a given duration

size_assertion.description: Checks the length of the response content, in bytes.

selector.description: The selector is a string that point to the elements in the page. Several types of selector are supported: text, CSS, XPath... You can specify several selectors by adding multiple selector parameters to this action. The targeted element will match any of the selectors (OR operator).

timeout.description: Forces the timeout for that action in ms. By default the OpenBrowser defaultTimeout is used. Maximum value is 200000.

waitForNavigation_url.description: URL pattern targeted, ex:http://tricentis.com/.* . The URL being navigated to must match this pattern. Enables a wait for page navigation after this action has been executed.

waitForNavigation_timeout.description: If applicable, the navigation must occur within the specified timeout in ms. By default the OpenBrowser defaultNavigationTimeout is used. Enables a wait for page navigation after this action has been executed. Maximum value is 200000.

waitForNavigation_until.description: Allowed values are : LOAD, DOMCONTENTLOADED, NETWORKIDLE, COMMIT. Default value is LOAD. The navigation will be considered done when the specified state is reached. Enables a wait for page navigation after this action has been executed.

waitForDownload.description: Enable waiting for a download if the parameter is set to true. Default value is "false".

waitForDownload_path.description: The path where to save the downloaded file. Can include the filename, i.e : /home/my-downloads/my-downloaded-file.txt

waitForDownload_timeout.description: If applicable, the download must start within the specified timeout in ms. By default the OpenBrowser defaultNavigationTimeout is used. Maximum value is 200000. If the timeout is set to 0, the download will be waited indefinitely.

ignoreErrors.description: Set this option to true to ignore errors for this action. This is useful for handling conditional actions without having to resort to a "If...Then...Else" or a "Try...Catch" block. Default value is "false".

force.description: true or false. Forces the click, even if the target element is obscured by other elements. Default value is "false".

anyOf.description: Browser type, possible values are: chromium, firefox, webkit. Default value is "chromium".
Whether to run browser in headless mode.
Sets the default timeout for every action in ms. Default value is 30000, maximum value is 200000.

Resolution (width x height) of browser. Example: 1920x1080
Locale of the browser. Example: en-GB

browser_close.title: Action: Real Browser BrowserClose

anyOf.description: This parameter is only applicable when the action is in the Actions container (ignored otherwise). Default is false, the internal processes are persisted in the Virtual user instance to be reused from one iteration to another. Setting the value to true will ensure all external processes are closed and recreated for each iteration, at the cost of increasing the response time and CPU consumption of this CloseBrowser and the next OpenBrowser actions. Default value is "false".

browser_close.description: Real Browser action BrowserClose. Close the browser. This action is useful for avoiding stacking browser instances on a single VU. The recommended configurations is : If the OpenBrowser action is at the beginning of the ACTIONS container, put the CloseBrowser action at end of the ACTIONS container.

browser_mouse_over.description: Real Browser action BrowserMouseOver. Positions the mouse over the specified coordinates or element location. Scrolls the window when that position is out of the current viewport. Both parameters can be set at the same time, in that case the mouse will be positioned at the specified coordinates relative to the located element instead of the page origin.

You can specify several selectors by adding multiple sourceSelector parameters to this action. The targeted element will match any of the selectors (OR operator).

The target selector identifies where the element dragged should be dropped. The selector is a string that point to the elements in the page. Several types of selector are supported: text, CSS, XPath... You can specify several selectors by adding multiple targetSelector parameters to this action. The targeted element will match any of the selectors (OR operator).
A position relative to the top left corner of the source element where to perform the click initiating the drag action. Example : 200;350
A position relative to the top left corner of the target element where to release the click finalizing the drop action. Example : 200;350

The amount of pixels to scroll on the Y axis. Positive values emulate a scroll down and negative values a scroll top event. Default value is "0".

browser_capture_requests.title: Action: Real Browser BrowserCaptureRequests

anyOf.description: The regular expression to group the requests (the matching check is applied on the full request URL: scheme, host name, port number, path and URL parameters). Default value is ".*".
The URL to group the requests (excluding query parameters).
The resource type to group the requests (possible values are document, stylesheet, image, media, font, script, texttrack, xhr, fetch, eventsource, websocket, manifest, ping, other).

By default, only the requests sent over the network are captured (including the requests with 304 'Not Modified' response status since it includes network exchange). Set the value to true to capture also the requests locally loaded from the browser memory or disk cache (no network interaction). Default value is "false".
By default, failed requests (network errors, connection refused, etc.) are excluded from captured results. Set the value to true to include them. Default value is "false".

Mitigates thread hanging issues when accessing the request sizes. Regular expression applied to the full request URL: when a request URL matches, response sizes are not computed. Leave empty to compute sizes for all requests. Advanced parameter, hidden by default in NeoLoad GUI.

browser_capture_requests.description: Real Browser action BrowserCaptureRequests. Configure the capture of HTTP requests metrics for analysis purpose. It allows to capture the metrics (duration, TTFB, success...) of the requests sent and responses received between the browser and the server. By default when no regexp/url/resourceType parameter is specified, then all the HTTP request metrics are aggregated in a single group. When a matching criteria is defined (regexp/url/resourceType), the metrics of all HTTP requests matching it are aggregated in a group, and the non-matching one in a different group (for example with regexp (.*)\.html then requests will be split in two different groups: one for all HTML pages and another one for all other resources). When multiple matching criteria are defined (regexp/url/resourceType), they are applied in order they are defined.

browser_capture_web_vitals.title: Action: Real Browser BrowserCaptureWebVitals

anyOf.description: A url (excluding query parameters) to group Web Vitals metrics data under.

browser_capture_web_vitals.description: Real Browser action BrowserCaptureWebVitals. Captures Core Web Vitals metrics during Virtual User navigation. This helps detect performance issues that affect the user experience. NeoLoad collects the following metrics for each defined URL: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). If you don't define a URL, NeoLoad aggregates metrics across all visited pages. To collect all metrics, place this action before the first Navigate action. The Virtual User needs to stay a minimum amount of time and perform at least one interaction to ensure Web Vitals were collected for a given page.
